result.note: Tested the terms of the March 2026 US waiver on Iranian oil at sea and its precedent with Russian oil; skipped the refiners' unconfirmed plans.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, the US issued a temporary sanctions waiver on Iranian oil amid the US-Israeli-Iranian conflict. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It covers Iranian oil already at sea that was loaded on or before 20 March 2026 and discharged by 19 April 2026.
It was the first time the US temporarily waived oil sanctions during the conflict.
Earlier temporary waivers during the conflict covered Russian oil already at sea.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The story calls this the third temporary US waiver of oil sanctions during the war, after earlier waivers for Russian oil already at sea. Analysts estimate the 30-day waiver covers roughly 170 million barrels on water. That volume is enough to ease shortages but not to bring prices down sharply.
questions.source: This marks the third time the US has temporarily waived oil sanctions during this war, having previously issued temporary waivers for Russian oil already at sea.
